back: An ordered arrangement of objects: changing the order gives a different permutation.

front: Number of permutations of r from n
back: $^{n}P_{r} = \dfrac{n!}{(n - r)!} = n(n - 1)\cdots(n - r + 1)$ (not in the List of formulas).

front: Arranging n distinct objects in a line

back: Treat them as one block; arrange the block with the rest, then multiply by the arrangements inside the block (e.g. $2!$).

front: Items that must not be together
back: Total arrangements minus the arrangements with them together.
Fill the restricted place first: last digit for odd/even, first digit for size. Use cases when one digit affects both.
Permutation when order or different roles matter (prizes, captain/vice-captain); combination for plain selections (teams, committees).
Repeated objects, circular arrangements, and problems needing both permutations and combinations.
